transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on dishes usually mean water isn't getting sprayed properly because something is blocking the flow. The most common cause is a filter that needs cleaning, followed by blocked spray arm holes. Please take out the lower rack and twist to lift out the filter at the bottom of the tub. Is it clogged with food or grit (and have you rinsed it clean), or was it already fairly clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok found the filter, its full of food n grease. will clean it now

That explains it perfectly—a filter choked with food and grease stops water from reaching the spray arms properly, which is why you're seeing gritty residue on your dishes. Please rinse that filter thoroughly under a tap until the water runs clear, then give each spray arm a spin by hand to ensure they turn freely and check that the tiny jet holes aren't blocked with grit. If an arm feels stuck or the jets are clogged, clear them out (a cocktail stick works well for the holes). Once everything is clean and moving freely, run a normal wash cycle and let me know if the dishes come out clean.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok filter rinsed. lower spray arm spins fine but the upper one is stiff. several holes on it were blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick. will run a normal cycle now

Good work clearing those jets. It is possible the arm might still be a bit stiff from the limescale, but running it should show us immediately. Please run that normal cycle and let me know if the dishes come out clean now, or if you still see grit.
ran a normal cycle and its much better, glasses n bowls look clean now

That is excellent news. The gritty residue was most likely caused by the blocked upper spray arm and the dirty filter restricting water flow. To help prevent this from happening again, try scraping off large food scraps before loading and give the filter a quick rinse every few weeks. If you need any further advice in the future, just let me know.
